concepts.title: Nature of Motivation: Needs, Drives and Goals
concepts.definition: Motivation is the internal process that energises, directs and sustains behaviour toward a goal. It begins with a need -- biological or psychological -- whose arousal creates a drive that pushes the organism into action until the goal reduces the tension. Motivation thus explains both the vigour and the direction of conduct.
concepts.key_idea: Need creates drive, drive fuels action, goal ends it -- motivation is the engine and steering of behaviour.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy108.txt motivation sections (nature of human motivation, needs drives goals, energising and directing behaviour)
question_patterns: define motivation and explain its cycle from need to goal

why do two people behave differently for the same goal
identify the need and goal in a given piece of behaviour

solution_steps.explain: Trace any sustained behaviour back to a need -- hunger, achievement, affiliation.
The aroused need creates tension that energises and directs activity toward satisfaction.
Reaching the goal reduces the drive and the behaviour subsides -- until the need arises again.

concepts.title: Types of Motives: Biological and Psychosocial
concepts.definition: Motives divide into biological needs -- hunger, thirst, sex, sleep -- rooted in the body's requirements, and psychosocial motives learned in society -- achievement, affiliation, power and curiosity. The former are shared with all animals and cycle with the body; the latter vary with culture and individual history.
concepts.key_idea: Body-built motives and society-taught motives -- hunger pushes everyone, achievement pushes differently.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy108.txt motives sections (important motives, hunger thirst, achievement motivation affiliation power curiosity, biological and psychosocial motives)
question_patterns: distinguish biological motives from psychosocial motives with examples

solution_steps.explain: Hunger, thirst and sleep arise from tissue needs and follow bodily cycles.
Achievement, affiliation, power and curiosity are learned, vary across persons and cultures, and drive long-term striving.
Social settings modulate even biological motives -- eating by the clock is culture bending biology.

concepts.title: Nature of Emotions and Their Expression
concepts.definition: Emotions are complex feeling states -- subjective experience, bodily arousal and expressive behaviour together -- that evaluate events as good or bad for us. They are expressed through facial expressions, posture and voice, read widely across cultures, and they energise, direct and even disrupt thought and action.
concepts.key_idea: Emotion is a three-part signal -- felt, aroused and shown -- that appraises the world and mobilises us.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy108.txt emotion sections (nature of emotional expression, facial expressions, cultural similarity in expression, arousal, functions of emotions)
question_patterns: define emotion and list its components

distinguish emotions from motives with an example

solution_steps.explain: An emotion joins subjective feeling, physiological arousal and outward expression.
Faces, voice and posture broadcast states; basic expressions are recognised across cultures.
Emotions appraise events, prepare responses and communicate -- mobilising or disrupting behaviour by intensity.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student studies late every night to top the board exams. Identify the motive involved and classify it.

solution_template.explain: Striving for excellence in competitive goals is achievement motivation.
It is a psychosocial motive -- learned, culture-shaped, and varying in strength across people.
Each success raises the bar and re-arms the motive -- unlike a bodily need, it is never finally satisfied.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Before a stage performance a singer's hands tremble and heart races, yet she sings better than usual. Explain using the nature of emotions.

solution_template.explain: Stage fright shows the full triad: subjective anxiety, bodily arousal and visible expression.
Moderate arousal sharpens attention and energises performance -- emotion preparing action.
Beyond a point the same arousal would disrupt her -- intensity decides whether emotion helps or harms.
